input: Run a KYC screen on Adyen in the Netherlands

output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-11-09, the provisional KYC rating is medium. Adyen N.V. is an identifiable, active Dutch entity and DNB-registered bank, with publicly disclosed governance. The entity-specific litigation located does not establish financial misconduct by Adyen: it was the victim in the SEPA fraud judgment dated 2024-05-08, Solitary's claims were rejected on 2025-06-11, and Shankar's case was dismissed procedurally in January 2025. No confirmed sanctions designation or PEP finding was established, but this is not a complete clearance: the retrieved sanctions versions have different update dates, current ultimate beneficial ownership was not verified, Goldman Sachs' OFAC screening was not completed, and historical holding-vehicle name overlaps remain unresolved. AFM positions below are dated disclosures, not proof of current beneficial ownership or control. The 12 excluded candidates comprise 10 sanctions name collisions and two litigation records whose exact-entity connection was not independently established. Missing_fields: direct KvK company/UBO extract; verified current beneficial owners/PSC and complete ownership-control chain; completed sanctions resolution for historical holding vehicles and Goldman Sachs' OFAC check; nationalities of Hwa Tsao, Herna Verhagen, Chris Vogelzang and A.D. Schuijff; registry numbers of related entities other than Adyen International B.V.; and any later appeal or reopening status of the reported proceedings.

Adyen returned eight fuzzy matches: six ADEN individuals, ISLAMIC ARMY OF ADEN, and the vessel AYDEN. These were excluded because their names and party types do not identify the Dutch company. BlackRock returned BLACK ROCK, a vessel, and Blacks, an individual, neither identifying BlackRock Inc. Searches for Pieter van der Does, Arnout Schuijff and T. Rowe Price returned no results. These name checks do not establish ownership-based sanctions clearance.

adverse_media.status: Judgment ordered defendants to repay the amounts received, with statutory interest. The court found no contributory fault by Adyen. Later appeal status not verified.
adverse_media.summary: Adyen N.V. was the plaintiff and victim of SEPA direct-debit fraud between 2023-01-20 and 2023-02-02. The judgment states that Adyen had advanced more than EUR 2,647,415 and sought recovery. This is operational fraud exposure, not a finding that Adyen committed fraud.

adverse_media.status: Dismissed on 2025-01-24 because the plaintiff did not pay the filing fee; judgment entered 2025-01-27. Later reopening or appeal status not verified.
adverse_media.summary: Shankar v. Adyen NV was filed in the Northern District of Illinois. The opened docket identifies Adyen NV as defendant but does not provide enough detail to characterize the substantive allegations. The procedural dismissal is not a merits finding against Adyen.

adverse_media.status: Amsterdam District Court rejected all Solitary claims and awarded costs against Solitary. Later appeal status not verified.
adverse_media.summary: Solitary B.V. sued Adyen N.V. over alleged breaches of duties and misuse of contractual powers concerning the deposit level for Athlete's payment services. The court did not find that Adyen had breached its contract or acted unlawfully.
adverse_media.category: Commercial litigation; alleged breach of duty

citations.title: Governance - Adyen
excerpts: ## Pieter van der Does Co-founder and Co-CEO With over two decades of experience in the payments industry, Pieter van der Does, was CCO at Bibit before co-founding Adyen in 2006. Since then, Adyen has grown from a startup into a globally operating business, averaging double-digit annual growth since 2007. Pieter built Adyen to transform the payments landscape, and has since solved payment complexity for many of the world’s leading businesses. He has earned a degree in Economics from the University of Amsterdam. ## Ingo Uytdehaage Co-CEO Ingo joined Adyen as the CFO in 2011 and was appointed as co-CEO in 2023. Before joining Adyen, he gained extensive experience in the field of finance at several large enterprises. Having earned two business degrees and held multiple managerial positions, Ingo plays an essential role in Adyen’s continued growth. He has earned degrees in accounting and finance from Maastricht University and followed the CPA post-graduate program from the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam. Ingo is a member of the Non-Executive Board of Vinted. ## Roelant Prins CCO As the Chief Commercial Officer of Adyen, Roelant is responsible for all commercial activities and development. After starting his career as a consultant, he moved on to the online payments industry in early 2000. Throughout the years, Roelant has held various international management roles in sales and business development for companies providing payment solutions to international ecommerce businesses. He has earned a degree in Economics from Erasmus University Rotterdam. Roelant is a member of the Supervisory Board of Seenons B.V. ## Mariëtte Swart CRCO Mariëtte is the Chief Risk and Compliance Officer of Adyen. Prior to this role, she was Adyen’s General Counsel and built the legal team from the ground up. Before joining Adyen, Mariëtte worked at an international law firm where she gained vast experience in global financial services, helping companies with products in payments, debt and equity solutions, M&A and financial markets. She has earned a degree in Regulated Markets and Corporate Law from Utrecht University. ## Brooke Nayden CHRO Brooke is the Chief Human Resources Officer at Adyen. Brooke has spent her career helping tech companies scale throughout high-growth phases, and brings a comprehensive understanding of the talent landscape to Adyen’s Management Board. At Adyen, Brooke served as Global Head of HR as part of the Global Leadership team, a role in which she successfully led the company’s expansion. Previously at Atlassian, she focused on Technical and Leadership Recruitment. Brooke holds a degree in History and Literature from Claremont McKenna College. ## Tom Adams CTO Tom is the Chief Technology Officer of Adyen. Prior to joining Adyen, he led the global engineering organization at Cash App (Block, Inc.). Tom has held senior leadership positions in various financial services and technology companies in the United States and Australia. With over 25 years of experience in technical and leadership roles, he brings significant leadership experience in high-growth technology companies. Tom holds a Bachelor of Information Technology in Computer Science and a Bachelor of Science in Physical Mathematics from Griffith University. ## Hwa Tsao Interim CFO As interim Chief Financial Officer of Adyen, Hwa Tsao is responsible for the company’s financial operations and continuity throughout the transition towards a permanent CFO. Before taking on this role, Hwa served as Adyen's Senior Vice President, Group Finance. His scope included Accounting and Control, Tax, Strategic Finance and Revenue Analytics, Financial Planning and Analysis, Pricing, Finance Data and Technology, and Investor Relations. He brings more than 20 years of senior finance experience, having held leadership roles at ServiceNow, and HP Inc. Earlier in his career, Hwa worked in Mergers and Acquisitions at Citigroup. Hwa holds a Bachelors degree and Juris Doctor from the University of Michigan, an LLM in Taxation from the New York University School of Law, as well as an MBA from the UCLA Anderson School of Management. Hwa is not a member of the statutory board.
